sentences.text: Squatinactis was an extinct cartilaginous fish with a flattened body and a set of large pectoral fins, known from the Carboniferous-aged Bear Gulch Limestone in Montana.
Its broad pectoral fins pointed forward and measured around two feet in length, resembling those of modern stingrays and angel sharks.
The animal had a short snout and a wide mouth containing long, conical, cladodont-shaped teeth, with the holotype specimen possessing approximately 15 teeth in its jaw.
The body of Squatinactis was covered in only a few placoid scales, leaving most of the surface bare.
Squatinactis is classified within the Elasmobranchii, specifically in its own order, Squatinactiformes.
Squatinactis lived during the Serpukhovian stage, between 326.9 and 323.6 million years ago.
It was likely a benthic predator that lived half-buried in the sand and lunged at nearby prey.
The wing-like fins and long tail were likely used for propulsion while moving along the seabed.
